title: Invoice finalization — the contract this interview settles

masthead.headline: Eleven answers decide the API contract, not the implementation.
masthead.lede: Each question below changes what the endpoint may promise. Nothing is locked until you answer; every untouched recommendation stays marked unresolved in the single reply.

sections.label: Execution
sections.title: May finalization finish after the request returns?

blocks.text: A synchronous answer removes the queue, the job record, the progress UI, the replay controls, and the on-call path. An asynchronous answer creates all five. The current p95 is 18 seconds; PDF rendering has reached 74 seconds on 400-line invoices.

blocks.label: Execution boundary
blocks.ask: What experience should the API promise once the invoice is submitted?

choices.summary: Return a job ID, expose progress, and notify when the immutable invoice is ready.
Simpler state model, but large invoices can exceed the gateway limit.
Commit accounting now; render the PDF and send email later.

blocks.label: Tolerated wait before the caller gets an ID
blocks.ask: How long may the synchronous part of finalization take before the caller is handed a job ID?

blocks.title: Why this question is first
blocks.text: Deferring this answer blocks the API response contract and the storage model. Every question below assumes work may be retried.

sections.label: Identity
sections.title: What makes two attempts the same business action?

rows.text: Request view
One click, one submission: a user presses Finalize once and expects one invoice.
Deduplicate on user intent
System reality
Three repeatable effects: persist ledger entry, reserve invoice number, deliver email.
Each effect needs its own checkpoint
Naive retry
A retried worker re-runs all three effects from the top.
Duplicate invoice numbers and duplicate email

blocks.label: Idempotency identity
blocks.ask: Which stable identity should suppress duplicate effects?

choices.summary: Survives request and worker retries; one key owns every effect.
Rejects stale retries but makes every edit a new operation.
Deduplicates workers, not duplicate submissions before a job exists.

blocks.label: Effects the identity must guard
blocks.ask: Which effects must be suppressed on a retry that carries the same identity?

options.summary: A gap or a duplicate is externally visible and auditable.
A second copy is visible to the customer and cannot be recalled.
Idempotent by content hash; re-rendering costs money, not correctness.
The partner deduplicates, but only within its own window.

sections.label: Recovery
sections.title: How much history must operators be able to replay?

items.title: Attempt recorded
items.text: Persist the input hash and the effect checkpoints before execution begins.

items.title: Partial failure
items.text: Email can fail after accounting and the invoice-number reservation have already succeeded.

items.title: Operator replay
items.text: Resume only the unfinished effects, under the same idempotency identity.

blocks.label: Replay retention
blocks.ask: How long should the input and effect ledger remain replayable?

choices.summary: Separates the executable payload's retention from the financial evidence.
Maximum recoverability with a much larger sensitive-data surface.
Lowest operator surface; unresolved partial failures require engineering.

blocks.label: Operator autonomy on replay
blocks.ask: How much may an operator replay without an engineer present?

sections.label: Ownership
sections.title: Who owns a job that is moving but producing the wrong outcome?

blocks.text: Queue health and invoice correctness are different incidents with different responders. Naming one owner for both means the queue's symptoms page the team that cannot read the ledger.

blocks.label: Incident ownership
blocks.ask: Who is paged when the queue is healthy but the invoices are wrong?

choices.summary: Billing owns stuck or incorrect invoices; platform owns queue saturation and delivery availability.
One accountable owner, including queue-level symptoms.
Centralizes operations, but detaches invoice correctness from its domain owner.

blocks.label: Runbook handoff
blocks.ask: Where does the handoff between those two owners have to be explicit, and who writes it down?
blocks.placeholder: e.g. platform escalates to billing once the queue drains but the ledger still shows unfinished effects

sections.label: Failure
sections.title: When does delayed work become an incident?

blocks.title: Consequence before threshold
blocks.text: A latency number is meaningful only when it is tied to a user or operational consequence. If the team cannot name the consequence, preserve the threshold as unresolved rather than inventing a latency target.

blocks.label: First page-worthy consequence
blocks.ask: Describe the first consequence that should page an operator.
blocks.placeholder: e.g. a customer has been charged but has no invoice document twenty minutes later

blocks.label: Signals that may page
blocks.ask: Which signals are allowed to page, once the consequence above is named?

options.value: Unfinished effects past the promised window
Invoice-number reservation without a ledger entry

options.summary: A symptom, not a consequence — page only if it predicts one.

blocks.label: Anything this interview cannot settle
blocks.ask: What still has to be measured or decided elsewhere before the contract can be written?

sections.label: Synthesis
sections.title: Read the contract these answers create together

blocks.text: The rows below show the contract created by the recommended path. Your confirmed overrides and untouched recommendations are carried separately in the reply, so the coder can tell a decision from a default.

rows.text: Execution
Submission and completion are separate states.
Job resource, progress query, completion notification
Effect identity
One user intent owns every retried effect.
Persist the idempotency key and per-effect checkpoints
Recovery
Replay data and audit evidence have different lifetimes.
Expiring payload plus a durable outcome ledger
Ownership
Business and infrastructure incidents route separately.
Two alert classes with an explicit runbook handoff

blocks.title: Knowledge gate
blocks.text: The reply is ready only when the page-worthy consequence is explicit. Until then it ships as an open question, not as a latency target nobody agreed to.
